dem.name: LROC NAC DTM NAC_DTM_CRISHORSE_E186N0618.IMG (4.0 m), 3 m site window

assumptions: Observer 2 m above the terrain at 18.5620, 61.8100 (degrees, east-positive, ME frame); heights above the 1737.4 km sphere.
Positions are topocentric and airless (no refraction), as JPL Horizons APPARENT=AIRLESS for a coord@301 observer.

Skyline from elevation data, including the Moon's curvature, 0.5 deg in azimuth, searched to 229 km: LROC NAC DTM NAC_DTM_CRISHORSE_E186N0618.IMG (4.0 m), 3 m site window (4 m) from 0.0 to 1.1 km; SLDEM2015 512 ppd, 60 m site window (60 m) from 0.8 to 5.4 km; SLDEM2015 512 ppd, 480 m site window (480 m) from 3.9 to 43.4 km; LOLA whole-Moon grid, 16 px/deg (1895.21 m) from 30.8 to 229.2 km.
Sampled every 10 min; rise and set times refined to 10 s; the Sun and Earth are discs (visible fraction integrated across each disc).
Sunrise/sunset = first/last moment any part of the Sun stands above the skyline. Earthrise/Earthset = Earth's centre crossing the skyline.
Sunlight also counts Earth passing in front of the Sun (geometric discs; the faint light refracted by Earth's atmosphere is ignored).
Earth visibility is geometric line of sight only; it says nothing about a working radio link.
Slope over a 10 m baseline from LROC NAC DTM NAC_DTM_CRISHORSE_E186N0618.IMG (4.0 m), 3 m site window, 4 m: hazards smaller than the grid are not seen.

warnings: Elevation data at this point, finest first: LROC NAC DTM NAC_DTM_CRISHORSE_E186N0618.IMG (4.0 m), 3 m site window (4 m per sample, to about 0.77 km); SLDEM2015 512 ppd, 60 m site window (60 m per sample, to about 3.8 km); SLDEM2015 512 ppd, 480 m site window (480 m per sample, to about 31 km); LOLA whole-Moon grid, 16 px/deg (1.9 km per sample, whole Moon).
Beyond about 31 km from the site only the whole-Moon grid is available (1.9 km per sample), which smooths ridges narrower than that; distant skyline peaks can read slightly low.
Earth passes in front of the Sun during this window (2025-03-14 05:00 UTC): sunlight and darkness include it.
The longest darkness runs into the edge of the window: it is a lower bound.
